title: Brookside commit: throughput & SLO mapping

Brookside commit: throughput & SLO mapping

['From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@brookside.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Brookside commit: throughput & SLO mapping

Hi Evan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To get our Dedicated sizing recommendation ready for the commercial proposal, could you confirm a couple of production numbers so we can model tokens/sec and headroom accurately?

Quick asks:
- Peak concurrent requests/sec (peak QPS) you expect at launch vs. steady-state?
- Average tokens generated per request (and 90/95 quantiles if you have them)?
- Target p95 latency SLO for the user request (end-to-end generation time you want Redwood to meet)?
- Any planned traffic patterns (quiet hours, batch windows, or predictable daily peaks)?

If easier, reply inline and I’ll convert to a run-rate and a conservative GPU recommendation. We’ll attach a spreadsheet with our assumptions once I have your numbers.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com

', 'From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@brookside.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Brookside commit: throughput & SLO mapping

Rachel — thanks, happy to confirm.

Inline answers below:
- Peak QPS: ~48 req/sec at launch peak (we see short spikes up to ~65 req/sec during marketing bursts). Steady-state (business hours) ~22 req/sec.
- Tokens per request: mean ~310 tokens; median ~280; 95th ~520. Most requests are a 1–2 paragraph generation.
- p95 latency SLO: target 750ms (end-to-end generation time is critical for UX; would accept 850ms max for peak windows).
- Traffic patterns: predictable daily peak 09:00–11:30 PST; lighter outside 20:00–06:00. Marketing-driven bursts can last 5–15 minutes.

Let me know if you need the sample traces — can share a short log export.

—Evan
Evan Liu
Head of Platform, Brookside AI
evan.liu@brookside.ai
', "From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@brookside.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Brookside commit: throughput & SLO mapping

Karthik / Laura — forwarding Brookside's numbers. Evan sent peak 48 req/s (spikes to 65), avg 310 tokens/req, p95 SLO 750ms (850ms acceptable in bursts).

Preliminary calc (quick notes):
- Peak token rate: 65 req/s * 520 tokens/req (use 95th for burst sizing) ≈ 33,800 tokens/sec (burst).
- Steady-state token rate: 48 req/s * 310 ≈ 14,880 tokens/sec (operational peak).

We typically map tokens/sec to GPU capacity using conservative per-GPU throughput numbers depending on model variant. Using the model they demoed (open-instruct-13B, optimized quantized path) our bench shows ~5,000 tokens/sec sustained per A100-equivalent GPU at SLO-friendly batching/latency profiles. For p95 <= 750ms we factor in batch sizing and KV cache warm-up which reduces effective throughput by ~10–15% initially.

Rough GPU sizing:
- Steady/operational peak (14,880 tps): 14,880 / 5,000 ≈ 2.98 → round to 3 GPUs.
- Burst headroom to absorb spike (33,800 tps): 33,800 / 5,000 ≈ 6.76 → ~7 GPUs.
- Apply a targeted headroom strategy: propose a Reserved slab = 4 GPUs (covers steady with ~33% headroom) + burst pool (autoscale/burst capacity) up to 7 GPUs.

Questions for you both:
1) For commercial, do we want the proposal to commit to a slab of 4 GPUs with a documented burst allowance (pay-as-you-go for extra)? That reduces customer commit and gives them explicit SLO behavior.
2) Karthik: do we have a discount band for a 12-month reserved commit in this range (equivalent tokens/month ~ computeable — I'll attach the spreadsheet)?

I've attached a draft capacity workbook (brookside_capacity_model.xlsx) with the calcs and a short PDF mapping p95 latency to GPU counts. Please poke holes.

Thanks — I want to align before I send a formal note back to Evan with exact commitment language.

Rachel
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[original message above]", 'From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Brookside numbers — commit sizing suggestion

Thanks Rachel — good work pulling numbers. A few thoughts from commercial/ops lens:

1) Pricing / commit framing: for a 12-month reserved slab of 4 GPUs we can offer a 22% discount off list. For anything beyond the slab (burst up to 7 GPUs), bill at on-demand with usage caps. That keeps their committed cost predictable while giving them burst protection.

2) Safety buffer and SLA: recommend we document an SLO table in the contract: p95 <= 750ms for steady-state (as defined: sustained 5-minute window <= 48 req/s and <= 15k tokens/sec); for short bursts (<= 15 minutes up to 65 req/s) we guarantee p95 <= 850ms provided burst capacity is available — otherwise fallback to queued/backoff semantics.

3) Operational recommendations:
- Enable prefix/KV caching for hotspot prompts (should reduce tokens generated on repeat requests by ~20% in practice).
- Warm-up policy: schedule a 5–10 minute warm-up job after deploy to fill KV cache and cold weights for the most common prompts.
- Autoscale warm pool: keep 1 hot standby node for fastest ramp (reduces cold-start tail latency).

4) Token commitment estimate (for billing): using expected steady throughput ~15k tokens/sec and 30% utilization factor for business hours, crude monthly token estimate ≈ 1.2B tokens/month. Recommend we propose two tiers: 1.0B/month and 1.5B/month commitments to match their growth plan.

If LAURA can sanity-check the 5k tokens/sec per-GPU assumption for the exact model and quantization we used, we can finalize numbers and I’ll draft the commercial template.

Karthik
Head of Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

', 'From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@brookside.ai>, procurement@brookside.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Brookside commit: throughput & SLO mapping — proposal summary and next steps

Evan / Brookside procurement team —

Thanks for the quick replies and context. Per our internal sizing discussion, here is the proposed Dedicated commit and operational plan we recommend for launch and early growth:

Executive summary (what we’re proposing)
- Reserved slab: 4 A100-equivalent GPUs (Reserved monthly capacity / Dedicated) — covers operational peak with ~33% steady headroom.
- Burst pool: autoscale up to 7 GPUs (on-demand billing for the delta) to absorb marketing-driven spikes up to ~65 req/s, with documented burst SLA behavior.
- Suggested commitment tiers (tokens/month): 1.0B / month or 1.5B / month (recommended starting point: 1.0B with option to bump at 90-day review).
- Pricing: 12-month reserved slab with 22% discount, on-demand pricing applies for burst usage beyond reserved slab.

SLOs and operational notes
- p95 latency guarantee: <= 750ms for steady-state (defined as sustained 5-minute windows <= 48 req/s and <= 15k tokens/sec).
- Burst window guarantee: <= 850ms for bursts up to 15 minutes and <= 33.8k tokens/sec provided autoscale capacity is available — otherwise we will apply graceful backoff semantics and notify your traffic manager.
- Recommended mitigations: KV/prefix caching, warm-up job post-deploy, 1-node hot-standby for fast ramp.

Attachments and links
- brookside_capacity_model.xlsx — detailed per-minute token/run calculations and per-GPU throughput assumptions.
- slo_latency_profiles.pdf — diagram linking token/sec bands to GPU counts and expected p95 latency.
- proposed_commit_summary.pdf — short commercial summary for procurement.
- HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Next steps
1) Evan / procurement: confirm whether Brookside prefers the 1.0B/mo or 1.5B/mo commitment band and any PO / billing requirements.
2) Karthik / Rachel: we’ll prepare the 12-month term sheet and DocuSign link once Brookside confirms tier.
3) Ops (Laura): please capture any model-specific per-GPU throughput updates and update the workbook; I’ll share an updated spreadsheet after your check.

Evan — happy to hop on a quick call to walk this through with your infra and procurement teams. Would Thursday 10:00–11:00 PT work?

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
